On the simulator a blind solve costs 0.04 s so the coin-flip is invisible; on a real rig blind ASTAP is tens of seconds vs a few for hinted and is the case that can lock the wrong field, so half the annotate/centering solves would pay the blind cost while holding a good position hint. refuted.claim: efix-autopilot-night WE-SEQ-N1: `SchedulerEngine._reconcileDispatchedRun` re-arms the autopilot — `ownsRun == false && hasActiveRun == false` clears `currentTargetId` so the next eligible tick dispatches again; the operator-takeover branch only 'keeps hysteresis'.
refuted.how: Adjacent input: the takeover is observed FIRST, then the operator's run ends (the ordinary way a night goes: operator Stops the autopilot, runs a manual sequence, walks away). /tmp/nsdry/core/test/a_scheduler_takeover_test.dart drives the real SchedulerEngine with a SchedulerRunOwnership sink at HEAD: start -> dispatch #1; sink.activeRunId='operator-manual-run' -> one tick (correctly declines); sink.activeRunId=null (rig free, same target still eligible) -> three further ticks. Result: `dispatched.length == 1`, `status.currentTargetId == 1` — the autopilot never dispatches again for the rest of the night and still reports an Active target. Cause is in scheduler_engine.dart `_reconcileDispatchedRun`: it nulls `_dispatchedRunId` BEFORE the `_executorHasActiveRun()` branch, so on the takeover tick the ownership token is discarded while `currentTargetId` stays pinned; every later tick returns at `if (runId == null) return;` and the clear can never happen. The takeover branch's own log line ('keeping hysteresis') prints once, so a live log looks correct. The batch's pinned test stops at the takeover tick and never resumes the night.

refuted.claim: efix-stop-pipeline WD-SEQ-N1: the notice `"Sequence cancelled"` is the operator's Stop, so exact-matching it and routing to `NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped` (info, non-critical, no banner/toast/audible/push) is safe; 'anything else is a real fault and must survive'.
refuted.how: Adjacent input: a safety abort. `terminate_with()` (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/executor/trigger_context.rs:512-524) sets `is_cancelled` for EVERY ParkAndAbort trigger — WeatherUnsafe (triggers/trigger.rs:452+), dome/safety-monitor, dawn — and the node tree then ends `NodeStatus::Cancelled`, whose arm emits the byte-identical `ExecutorEvent::Error { message: "Sequence cancelled" }` (executor/start.rs:5216-5219). /tmp/nsdry/core/test/b_safety_abort_classification_test.dart feeds that exact wire event to `NotificationEventClassifier.classify` at HEAD: category = sequenceStopped, isCritical=false, defaultSeverity=info. So a weather/dome ParkAndAbort at 3am is now reported as 'Stopped by request' with no banner, no toast, no alarm — and per the batch's own note `sequenceStopped` is in `SystemPushTransport._pushSpecFor`'s `return null` arm, so no phone push either. The predicate is exact but the notice is not unique to the operator; the fix converted a cry-wolf into a silenced safety alert.

refuted.claim: efix-autopilot-night, Wave-E refutation of SEQ-13: `_syncTargetsAfterSnapshotSwap` on undo()/redo() means the builder tree and the `targets` row the scheduler scores can no longer diverge across an undo.

refuted.claim: E-fix WD-SEQ-N1 / WE-SEQ-N6: 'a stop is not an error' — reclassifying the sequencer Error carrying "Sequence cancelled" to sequenceStopped across all five producers is safe because the operator pressed the button.
refuted.how:
The premise is false for the majority of the ways that event is produced. native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/executor/start.rs:5218 emits `ExecutorEvent::Error { message: "Sequence cancelled" }` for EVERY NodeStatus::Cancelled root, and the cancel flag is set by executor/trigger_context.rs:512 `terminate_with()`, whose four call sites in start.rs are 3625 RecoveryAction::ParkAndAbort (the WeatherUnsafe / AltitudeLimit / TimeLimit safety triggers), 3887 AutofocusFailureAction::AbortAndPark, 4221 FlipFailureAction::AbortAndPark and 4911 CustomBranch-cancelled. In the healthy ParkAndAbort path NO ExecutorEvent::Error carrying the real cause is emitted (start.rs:3590-3628 only emits one when the mount is missing or the cover/dome failed to close), and triggers/trigger.rs:468 states outright that the cause goes to a tracing::warn! and nothing else. So a weather abort, a failed meridian flip that parked the scope, and an operator Stop are byte-identical on the wire.

All three E-fix producers now suppress escalation for that event: event_classifier.dart:141 -> sequenceStopped; run_dashboard_providers.dart:924-937 `continue`s past the critical bridge with the comment "no phone page for a button the operator just pressed"; event_operations.dart:252 replaces the message with "Stopped by request".

Proven with a throwaway test (/tmp scratchpad, package skotiq_core, both cases green): NotificationEventClassifier.classify(sequencer Error {'message':'Sequence cancelled'}) == NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped; and NotificationRoutingMatrix.defaults().ruleFor(sequenceStopped).transports does NOT contain NotificationTransportKind.systemPush, while ruleFor(sequenceFailed) does. system_push_transport.dart `_pushSpecFor` also returns null for sequenceStopped (line 189, the "intentionally does NOT escalate" group), so the drop is doubled — matrix and transport.

Net effect: before E-fix a meridian-flip AbortAndPark at 01:00 paged the sleeping operator at critical priority. After E-fix it produces no phone push, no critical banner, no toast, an info row in RECENT EVENTS, and copy that reads "Sequence stopped by request at 01:00" (notification_router.dart:593 default body) — the app asserting the operator requested a stop nobody requested. That is the campaign's own cry-wolf class inverted into cry-nothing. notification_categories.dart:103 even documents the intended behaviour as "An operator (or safety trigger) chose to stop: worth telling a phone" — the transport contradicts its own comment.

The batch tests miss it because every one of them (event_classifier_stop_vs_error_test.dart, operator_stop_outcome_test.dart, operator_stop_not_escalated_test.dart, run_stop_classification_producers_test.dart) frames the input as the operator's Stop and asserts only that it is not an error; none asserts that a run ended by a safety trigger still reaches the operator. Minimum repair: have the native distinguish the terminal (e.g. a distinct notice or a `reason` field on the Cancelled arm) so trigger-driven aborts keep a critical route, or route sequenceStopped to systemPush at normal priority so an unattended night-ender is never silent.

refuted.claim: E-fix 'every plan unparks first' (scheduler_engine.dart:546-552): adding an unconditional UnparkNode to every autopilot-generated plan is harmless because 'unparking an already-unparked mount is a no-op on every backend'.
refuted.how:
The no-op claim is true and irrelevant; what the change removes is an interlock. The commit's own comment names the three states it is defeating: 'its own dawn park, the weather watchdog and a manual park'. Two of those are safety states.

SchedulerEngine has no weather or safety gate at all — grep for weather/safe/isSafe/safetyMonitor across services/scheduler/*.dart and scheduler_engine/*.dart returns only comments and the dawn Sun-altitude check (_isEndOfNight, evaluation.dart:377). And _buildSequence (scheduler_engine.dart:494-575) attaches NO triggers to the generated Sequence — nodes are only Unpark/Slew/Center/Exposure — so an autopilot plan carries no in-sequence WeatherUnsafe ParkAndAbort either. The weather watchdog (providers/weather_safety/weather_safety_enforcement.dart) parks via SafeRigService and holds its own auto-resume holdoff; it never touches the scheduler.

So the only thing that stopped the autopilot imaging through unsafe weather was the parked mount making every dispatch die in 0 s at 'Slew: Mount is parked' — the exact symptom this change was written to eliminate. Concrete regression, and it is enabled by the SAME batch: the WeatherUnsafe trigger fires ParkAndAbort -> run ends Cancelled -> the executor settles -> _ExecutorSequenceSink.hasActiveRun (scheduler_engine_providers.dart:83) goes false -> the new _reconcileDispatchedRun (scheduler_engine.dart:302) clears currentTargetId because 'the rig is free' -> the next 60 s tick dispatches the same target -> UnparkNode unparks the weather-parked mount and slews under the unsafe sky, inside the enforcement layer's own resume holdoff. Repeat all night. The two E-fix commits compose into a park/unpark thrash that images through a storm.

No test in the batch covers it: scheduler_run_ended_redispatch_test.dart and scheduler_autopilot_ownership_test.dart both stub the sink and assert only ownership/redispatch, never a parked-for-safety mount. Minimum repair: gate the unpark on a safety verdict (or on the mount having been parked by the operator/dawn rather than by the watchdog), and give SchedulerEngine a weather/safety readiness gate before dispatch — SchedulerReadiness already has a `weather` member (models/scheduler/scheduler_readiness.dart:10) that nothing in the engine consults.

refuted.how: Adjacent input: the takeover is observed FIRST, then the operator's run ends (the ordinary way a night goes: operator Stops the autopilot, runs a manual sequence, walks away). /tmp/nsdry/core/test/a_scheduler_takeover_test.dart drives the real SchedulerEngine with a SchedulerRunOwnership sink at HEAD: start -> dispatch #1; sink.activeRunId='operator-manual-run' -> one tick (correctly declines); sink.activeRunId=null (rig free, same target still eligible) -> three further ticks. Result: `dispatched.length == 1`, `status.currentTargetId == 1` — the autopilot never dispatches again for the rest of the night and still reports an Active target. Cause is in scheduler_engine.dart `_reconcileDispatchedRun`: it nulls `_dispatchedRunId` BEFORE the `_executorHasActiveRun()` branch, so on the takeover tick the ownership token is discarded while `currentTargetId` stays pinned; every later tick returns at `if (runId == null) return;` and the clear can never happen. refuted.claim: E-fix WD-SEQ-N1 / WE-SEQ-N6: 'a stop is not an error' — reclassifying the sequencer Error carrying "Sequence cancelled" to sequenceStopped across all five producers is safe because the operator pressed the button.
refuted.how:
The premise is false for the majority of the ways that event is produced. native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/executor/start.rs:5218 emits `ExecutorEvent::Error { message: "Sequence cancelled" }` for EVERY NodeStatus::Cancelled root, and the cancel flag is set by executor/trigger_context.rs:512 `terminate_with()`, whose four call sites in start.rs are 3625 RecoveryAction::ParkAndAbort (the WeatherUnsafe / AltitudeLimit / TimeLimit safety triggers), 3887 AutofocusFailureAction::AbortAndPark, 4221 FlipFailureAction::AbortAndPark and 4911 CustomBranch-cancelled. In the healthy ParkAndAbort path NO ExecutorEvent::Error carrying the real cause is emitted (start.rs:3590-3628 only emits one when the mount is missing or the cover/dome failed to close), and triggers/trigger.rs:468 states outright that the cause goes to a tracing::warn! and nothing else. So a weather abort, a failed meridian flip that parked the scope, and an operator Stop are byte-identical on the wire.

All three E-fix producers now suppress escalation for that event: event_classifier.dart:141 -> sequenceStopped; run_dashboard_providers.dart:924-937 `continue`s past the critical bridge with the comment "no phone page for a button the operator just pressed"; event_operations.dart:252 replaces the message with "Stopped by request".

Proven with a throwaway test (/tmp scratchpad, package skotiq_core, both cases green): NotificationEventClassifier.classify(sequencer Error {'message':'Sequence cancelled'}) == NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped; and NotificationRoutingMatrix.defaults().ruleFor(sequenceStopped).transports does NOT contain NotificationTransportKind.systemPush, while ruleFor(sequenceFailed) does. system_push_transport.dart `_pushSpecFor` also returns null for sequenceStopped (line 189, the "intentionally does NOT escalate" group), so the drop is doubled — matrix and transport.

Net effect: before E-fix a meridian-flip AbortAndPark at 01:00 paged the sleeping operator at critical priority. After E-fix it produces no phone push, no critical banner, no toast, an info row in RECENT EVENTS, and copy that reads "Sequence stopped by request at 01:00" (notification_router.dart:593 default body) — the app asserting the operator requested a stop nobody requested. That is the campaign's own cry-wolf class inverted into cry-nothing. notification_categories.dart:103 even documents the intended behaviour as "An operator (or safety trigger) chose to stop: worth telling a phone" — the transport contradicts its own comment.

The batch tests miss it because every one of them (event_classifier_stop_vs_error_test.dart, operator_stop_outcome_test.dart, operator_stop_not_escalated_test.dart, run_stop_classification_producers_test.dart) frames the input as the operator's Stop and asserts only that it is not an error; none asserts that a run ended by a safety trigger still reaches the operator. Minimum repair: have the native distinguish the terminal (e.g. a distinct notice or a `reason` field on the Cancelled arm) so trigger-driven aborts keep a critical route, or route sequenceStopped to systemPush at normal priority so an unattended night-ender is never silent.

refuted.claim: E-fix 'every plan unparks first' (scheduler_engine.dart:546-552): adding an unconditional UnparkNode to every autopilot-generated plan is harmless because 'unparking an already-unparked mount is a no-op on every backend'.
refuted.how:
The no-op claim is true and irrelevant; what the change removes is an interlock. The commit's own comment names the three states it is defeating: 'its own dawn park, the weather watchdog and a manual park'. Two of those are safety states.

SchedulerEngine has no weather or safety gate at all — grep for weather/safe/isSafe/safetyMonitor across services/scheduler/*.dart and scheduler_engine/*.dart returns only comments and the dawn Sun-altitude check (_isEndOfNight, evaluation.dart:377). And _buildSequence (scheduler_engine.dart:494-575) attaches NO triggers to the generated Sequence — nodes are only Unpark/Slew/Center/Exposure — so an autopilot plan carries no in-sequence WeatherUnsafe ParkAndAbort either. The weather watchdog (providers/weather_safety/weather_safety_enforcement.dart) parks via SafeRigService and holds its own auto-resume holdoff; it never touches the scheduler.

So the only thing that stopped the autopilot imaging through unsafe weather was the parked mount making every dispatch die in 0 s at 'Slew: Mount is parked' — the exact symptom this change was written to eliminate. Concrete regression, and it is enabled by the SAME batch: the WeatherUnsafe trigger fires ParkAndAbort -> run ends Cancelled -> the executor settles -> _ExecutorSequenceSink.hasActiveRun (scheduler_engine_providers.dart:83) goes false -> the new _reconcileDispatchedRun (scheduler_engine.dart:302) clears currentTargetId because 'the rig is free' -> the next 60 s tick dispatches the same target -> UnparkNode unparks the weather-parked mount and slews under the unsafe sky, inside the enforcement layer's own resume holdoff. Repeat all night. The two E-fix commits compose into a park/unpark thrash that images through a storm.

No test in the batch covers it: scheduler_run_ended_redispatch_test.dart and scheduler_autopilot_ownership_test.dart both stub the sink and assert only ownership/redispatch, never a parked-for-safety mount. Minimum repair: gate the unpark on a safety verdict (or on the mount having been parked by the operator/dawn rather than by the watchdog), and give SchedulerEngine a weather/safety readiness gate before dispatch — SchedulerReadiness already has a `weather` member (models/scheduler/scheduler_readiness.dart:10) that nothing in the engine consults.
